chapter: Father and the brass band tradition
title: Brass band picnics and excursions
summary: His father played picnics, excursions and fairground dances with the brass band, never in small groups; Barbarin was once sick at a picnic.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: We talked to your father about a year ago, of course, but a lot of things we didn't ask him. It was a little difficult, you know, he couldn't hear something.
He was sick at the time, yeah.
But do you remember, did he ever play any dance bands at all, orchestra work, or just all these brass bands? Well, I'll tell you.
I played, we played picnics on the 30th of May. That'd be a big day in your, 10th of May, the 30th of May. And we played the picnics like the Seda, like the Vardalia's picnic, like that.

and excursions like that. My dad should go to King Oliver and then they'd play excursions out of Littlewood like that. And they'd go down for us to Point Lahash to have excursions, train excursions. And he'd also play picnics at the fairground like that. Set the big band up and see, and people would dance. With the brass band? With the brass band, by the brass band. That's correct. I played too. I played with the violi-dadi's picnics at the fairground and I was taking a sick tonight playing snare drum. Not taking a sick I ate some potatoes out of a galvanized tub they had there, you know, and ingesting it. Potato salad, what you call it.
That put you out of commission for that game. Huh? That put you out of commission for the rest of the game.
Oh yeah, for a while I really was out of commission. Was your father ever playing in any small groups, do you think, like a seven or eight piece No.
